title: Παῖς καὶ κόραξ
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 294. Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Μαντευομένης τινὸς περὶ τοῦ ἑαυτῆς παιδὸς νηπίου ὄντος, οἱ μάντεις προέλεγον ὅτι ὑπὸ κόρακος ἀναιρεθήσεται.
sentences.tr: Manteuomenēs tinos peri tou heautēs paidos nēpiou ontos, hoi manteis proelegon hoti hypo korakos anairethēsetai.
sentences.l: When a certain woman was consulting an oracle about her own child, who was an infant, the seers foretold that he would be killed by a raven.
sentences.n: The fable opens with a genitive absolute, Μαντευομένης τινός; that the enquirer is a woman shows only in ἑαυτῆς, 'her own'. μαντεύομαι is to consult a seer or an oracle, not to prophesy oneself. After προέλεγον the ὅτι-clause keeps the tense the prediction itself had — a future indicative where English shifts back to 'would'.

sentences.t: Διόπερ φοβουμένη λάρνακα μεγίστην κατασκευάσασα ἐν ταύτῃ αὐτὸν καθεῖρξε, φυλαττομένη μὴ ὑπὸ κόρακος ἀναιρεθῇ.
sentences.tr: Dioper phoboumenē larnaka megistēn kataskeuasasa en tautēi auton katheirxe, phylattomenē mē hypo korakos anairethēi.
sentences.l: Therefore, in fear, having had a very great chest made, she shut him up in it, taking care lest he be killed by a raven.
sentences.i: So in her fear she had a great chest built and shut him up inside it, taking care that no raven should kill him.
sentences.n: φυλάττομαι μή with the subjunctive is 'take care lest' — the construction of precaution, close cousin to the clause of fearing. λάρναξ is a chest or coffer, and the same word serves for a coffin.

sentences.t: Καὶ διετέλει τεταγμέναις ὥραις ἀναπεταννῦσα καὶ τὰς ἐπιτηδείους αὐτῷ τροφὰς παρεχομένη.
sentences.tr: Kai dietelei tetagmenais hōrais anapetannysa kai tas epitēdeious autōi trophas parechomenē.
sentences.l: And she went on, at appointed hours, throwing it open and providing him with the food suitable for him.
sentences.n: διατελέω with a supplementary participle says only that the action never stopped; the participles ἀναπεταννῦσα and παρεχομένη carry the doing. τεταγμέναις ὥραις is a dative of time, 'at set hours'.

sentences.t: Καί ποτε ἀνοιξάσης αὐτῆς καὶ τὸ πόμα ἐπιθείσης, ὁ παῖς ἀπροφυλάκτως παρέκυψεν.
sentences.tr: Kai pote anoixasēs autēs kai to poma epitheisēs, ho pais aprophylaktōs parekypsen.
sentences.l: And once, when she had opened it and was putting the lid on, the boy leaned out unguardedly.
sentences.n: Chambry prints πόμα, which is 'drink'; the word wanted is πῶμα, 'lid', and the two run together in the manuscripts. The printed form is kept. Both participles are aorist, but the sense is that the boy put his head out while she was setting the lid back in place.

sentences.t: Οὕτω τε συνέβη τῆς λάρνακος τὸν κόρακα κατὰ τοῦ βρέγματος κατενεχθέντα ἀποκτεῖναι αὐτόν.
sentences.tr: Houtō te synebē tēs larnakos ton koraka kata tou bregmatos katenechthenta apokteinai auton.
sentences.l: And so it came about that the raven of the chest, brought down upon the front of his head, killed him.
sentences.i: And so it came about that the chest's raven — the hooked catch of the lid — came down on his head and killed him.
sentences.n: The whole fable turns on a second sense of κόραξ: besides the bird it is the hooked catch, the 'raven', of a lid or a door. The prophecy came true through the fitting, not the bird. κατενεχθέντα is the aorist passive participle of καταφέρω agreeing with τὸν κόρακα, which is the accusative subject of ἀποκτεῖναι after συνέβη. βρέγμα is the front part of the head, the forehead and the bone above it. Chambry prints no moral here; the closing sentence is left to do that work.
